title: Bamboo, the giant grass
text:
Bamboo looks like a tree, but it is really a giant grass. It belongs to the same plant family as wheat, rice and the grass on a football pitch. There are more than a thousand kinds of bamboo, and they grow in Asia, Africa and the Americas.

Bamboo is famous for how fast it grows. Some kinds can grow almost a metre in a single day. It is amazing that a shoot can be taller than a child after only two days. Because it grows so quickly, bamboo can be cut again and again without killing the plant. The roots stay underground and send up new stems.

Bamboo stems are hollow, so they are light, but they are also strong. In Hong Kong, workers still build bamboo scaffolding around tall buildings, tying the poles together with strips of plastic. In Indonesia, craftspeople turn bamboo into musical instruments such as the angklung, as well as baskets and furniture. Young shoots are even cooked and eaten.

Bamboo is also an important food for wild animals. A giant panda can eat more than ten kilograms of bamboo every day.

Some scientists think that bamboo could replace a few plastic products, such as straws and toothbrushes. In my view, bamboo is the most useful plant in the world. Whether or not you agree, it is certainly a plant worth growing.
